dimensions.note: Values reach kubectl only as a base64 manifest on stdin, never on argv; kubeconfig and values are vault references (data is sensitive-marked) or are resolved by the model itself from data_from_vault through the runtime context.vaultService {get,put} object, tested through a plain-object context. Output and state carry metadata and key names only; per-key comparison hashes live in-process and are never returned or stored. kubectl stderr is never returned (fixed typed messages). Kubeconfig is default-deny: merge keys and tags refused up front, then canonicalized by kubectl config view --raw -o json and the canonical form validated (no exec/auth-provider plugins, no file-path credentials such as tokenFile or client-key) and written 0600 as the only kubeconfig kubectl uses. Live: value text in console output 0 across 22 cells. Residual MEDIUM (terra): if the selected cluster has no explicit server, the state-id fingerprint digests the whole kubeconfig (48 bits in the id). Residual MEDIUM (astra, delta): the optional() wrapper on data is not itself sensitive-marked (the inner record is). Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: README uses vault references only and never --json.
Each method logs once with name/status placeholders; no value, kubeconfig or kubectl output in log fields.

Typed K8sSecretError with fixed messages: API server unreachable, not authorized, namespace absent, kubectl failed, invalid input; vault lookup failures name the vault and key only. All live-verified (cells 8-13, V3-V4). Residual MEDIUM (terra): if the Secret is deleted between apply and the follow-up observe, state records present with no keys.

60 unit tests (secret 29, kubectl 12, kubeconfig 14, vault 5) with an injected runner, files and clock, including leak-regression tests, injected-IO temp-file cleanup, merge-key smuggles and a run against the real kubectl (tests need --allow-run=kubectl). data_from_vault is driven through a plain-object {get,put} context. Live end-to-end on a k0s single node: 14/14 on 073f868 plus 8/8 data_from_vault cells on 7dfcd38 (22/22).

Server-side apply with a per-definition field manager; no-op detection compares desired keys and values with the keys this field manager owns (managedFields), so external keys are preserved and dropped owned keys are pruned. Live: idempotent re-apply leaves resourceVersion unchanged (cells 3, V2); delete of an absent Secret is a clean no-op (cell 7). Residual MEDIUM (terra, raised HIGH and downgraded): two independent swamp repositories that give a definition the same name and target the same Secret share a field manager; that is an operator naming collision, not a single-orchestrator defect.

Built on kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f - and kubectl get -o json with clearEnv and an explicit KUBECONFIG; requires kubectl on PATH (README Install). The Deno.Command spawn of kubectl is accepted with an inline swamp-quality-ignore (every argument validated, documented).

Raw and canonical kubeconfigs are 0600 temp files removed in finally; a write/chmod failure removes the partial file (tested). Live: temp kubeconfigs left 0 after unreachable and bad-credential cells. data is bounded to 256 keys and 1 MiB total. Residual MEDIUM (astra, raised HIGH and downgraded): the cleanup loop stops if the first remove throws a non-NotFound error, which can leave the second 0600 temp file; the error surfaces, nothing is silent. Residual MEDIUM (terra, delta): data_from_vault values are all resolved before the total-byte check.

Manifest @randybias/k8s-secret 2026.10.17.1 (model version literal matches), Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt, LOGBOOK not packaged. apply description starts DESTRUCTIVE. Leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Residual LOW (astra): apply description runs four sentences; digestHex duplicates sha256Hex.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject. name/namespace are DNS-1123, context and type carry grammars, Secret keys follow the Kubernetes key rule and reject ., .. and __proto__ (null-prototype maps); exactly one of data or data_from_vault; vault and key names grammar-validated. Live: invalid key and 5 hostile name/namespace values each rejected before kubectl (cells 11, 12, V5-V7). Residual MEDIUM (astra): cluster server, proxy-url and tls-server-name accept any scalar (kubectl parses them).
apply (create/update), get, sync and delete; delete is kind action (run ruling 1: tombstoning follows kind delete, not the method name), live-verified including delete-again.
Arguments, kubeconfig shape and canonical kubeconfig are validated before any API call; namespace existence is reported with a typed error (cell 10).

State name combines a readable context_namespace_name with a 16-hex digest of a nonsecret cluster fingerprint (selected context's server) and the components, so a/b vs a_b and the same context in two clusters do not collide.
Methods read only this model's own state; kubeconfig and values arrive as method arguments or vault names, so one definition serves any cluster.
First release; no prior data to migrate.
